title: Credit Losses & Allowance Method
description: Estimate uncollectible receivables and record credit losses.
html:
Why do companies estimate credit losses?

When a company sells goods or services on credit, some customers may not pay what they owe.

Because of this, a company should consider expected credit losses on its receivables.

Allowance for Credit Losses

Instead of waiting until a specific customer fails to pay, the company estimates expected uncollectible amounts.

The estimate is recorded in an Allowance for Credit Losses, which is a contra-asset account related to receivables.

Net Accounts Receivable = Accounts Receivable − Allowance for Credit Losses

Example

Assume a company has:

Accounts Receivable $100,000
Allowance for Credit Losses ($4,000)
Net Accounts Receivable $96,000

Recording estimated credit losses

Suppose the company determines that its allowance needs to increase by $4,000.

Very important

Under the allowance method, the write-off itself generally does not create a new credit loss expense.

The expense was recognized when the expected loss was estimated.

Aging of receivables

Companies may estimate expected credit losses by grouping receivables according to how long they have been outstanding.

General idea

A receivable that is 120 days overdue may have a greater expected credit-loss percentage than a receivable that is only 10 days old.

quiz.prompt: Accounts Receivable is $80,000 and the Allowance for Credit Losses has a $5,000 credit balance. What is net Accounts Receivable?
quiz.explanation: Net Accounts Receivable equals $80,000 minus the $5,000 allowance, resulting in $75,000.
